item.title: Potential Health Benefits of Piceatannol-Rich Extracts from Passiflora edulis f. flavicarpa Seeds on Modulating Gene Expressions Related to Fat Metabolism and Muscle Development in C2C12 Myotubes
item.description:
Abstract
Yellow passion fruits are widely cultivated in many countries. Throughout industrial manufacturing operations, seeds are frequently disposed of as byproducts. Passion fruit seeds are an abundant natural source of piceatannol, which is known for its antioxidant properties and its ability to modulate protein turnover. This study investigated the potential benefits of passion fruit (PF) extract from pulp and juice, as well as piceatannol-rich (PIC) extract from passion fruit seeds, on palmitic acid (PA)-induced myosteatosis-related muscle atrophy in C2C12 myotubes at the transcriptional level. The PIC extract yielded 5.1% (w/w) with a piceatannol concentration of 0.37% (w/w). The result showed that the PIC extract was more effective in free radical scavenging than the piceatannol standard. Additionally, the results demonstrated that PA promoted lipid accumulation while impairing the muscle formation and glucose absorption. However, both PF and PIC extracts demonstrated a significant reduction in PA-induced lipid accumulation, accompanied by suppression of diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1 (Dgat1) expression without altering sirtuin 1 (Sirt1) and uncoupling protein 3 (Ucp3). In addition, both extracts tended to enhance the expression of myosin heavy chain 1 (Myh1) and glucose transporter type 4 (GLUT4), while markedly reducing myostatin (Mstn) expression, suggesting improvements in muscle development and glucose uptake. Furthermore, the PIC extract suppressed pancreatic lipase activity, which minimizes spikes in postprandial triglycerides in the blood circulation of rats. These findings emphasize the potential health benefits of PF and PIC extracts in enhancing glucose absorption and inhibiting fat synthesis in C2C12 myotubes, suggesting potential to mitigate lipid accumulation-related muscle development. The promising findings from cell culture suggest further in vivo investigation for studying their physiological relevance to muscle wasting caused by fat accumulation in obesity.

item.title: Cholesterol Reshapes Electroporation Energetics in Phosphatidylcholine Model Membranes
item.description:
Abstract
Cholesterol modulates membrane packing and mechanics, but how concentration reshapes the free-energy landscape from water-defect nucleation to pore expansion remains incompletely resolved. Here, all-atom molecular dynamics, a continuous joint pore coordinate, umbrella sampling under applied potentials, and unbiased direct-field trajectories were combined for a controlled 300 K DMPC/cholesterol series. Across the low-to-medium range, cholesterol increased the characteristic nucleation-region free-energy cost and pore-edge line tension while making metastable pore states shallower; increasing potential lowered hydrated-defect growth costs. Direct-field simulations at composition-specific operational pore-onset potentials separately showed composition-dependent channel timing and pore lifetimes, operationally defined by continuous-water connectivity. Matched DMPC, POPC, and DOPC membranes containing 20 mol % cholesterol showed lipid-dependent responses in nucleation-region profiles, core hydration, charge-density-derived relative electrostatic potentials, and pore structure. The 66 mol % DMPC system defined a distinct high-cholesterol response that departed from lower-concentration trends. Overall, electroporation emerged as a composition- and field-dependent remodeling of the poration landscape, with the matched 20 mol % systems further revealing lipid-dependent responses.

item.title: Microplastics (PP, PE, PS, and PVC) Induce Structural and Functional Changes in Digestive Enzymes: Insights from Spectroscopic Approaches
item.description:
Abstract
Exposure to microplastics (MPs) poses evolving health risks due to their interactions with biological systems; however, their mechanistic effects on digestive enzymes remain incompletely understood. This study employed in vitro structural and functional analyses, utilizing spectroscopic and enzyme inhibition assays, to investigate the impact of various simulated secondary postconsumer microplastics (PC-MPs) at a single concentration (714 μg/mL/day) on digestive enzymes, including α-amylase, pepsin, and pancreatin. Structural analysis was performed in a simulated digestive fluid system, examining fluorescence and circular dichroism (CD) spectra, including fluorophore quantum yield, quenching percentage, amino acid residue changes, aggregation and complex formation, and the percentage of protein secondary structural content. Functional analysis was conducted using enzyme activity inhibition assays. Comparative spectroscopic findings highlighted marked conformational changes and functional disruptions in digestive enzymes. Fluorescence and CD spectra, along with secondary structure analysis, revealed a consistent loss of emission from (Tyr and Trp) amino acid residues and α-helices and β-sheets, indicating potential destabilization. From the observation, it is evident that PP-MPs have a pronounced impact on α-amylase and pepsin, whereas PE-MPs affect the pancreatic enzyme mixtures. On the other hand, functional analysis revealed that PP-MPs strongly inhibited the activities of salivary α-amylase, pepsin, and pancreatic α-amylase, whereas PS-MPs inhibited pancreatic protease. In the present study, the PP-MPs had a substantial effect on salivary α-amylase and pepsin. In the case of PE- and PS-MPs, distinct differences were observed with pancreatin enzyme, possibly due to the mixture of enzymes contained. This study reveals that PC-MPs disrupt the structure of digestive enzymes and impair their activity, raising concerns about digestive health.

item.title: Gold-Enhanced Multielectrode Electrochemical Immunosensor for Rapid Electrochemical Detection of Dengue NS1
item.description:
Abstract
Dengue is one of the most widespread viral diseases in the world, transmitted mainly by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. In tropical and resource-limited regions, rapid and accurate diagnostic tools are of utmost importance, especially when aiming for effective control, but current detection methods face limitations in sensitivity, specificity, or accessibility. In this work, a multielectrode disposable electrochemical immunosensor was developed for the detection of the nonstructural protein 1 (NS1), an early biomarker of dengue infection. This device presents four fully individual and functional working electrodes modified with gold nanoparticles. This configuration enables replicate measurements and improved reproducibility within a single platform while using minimal sample volume. The electrodeposition of Au nanoparticles was optimized through Design of Experiments approaches, allowing the system to suitably determine the target protein with a specific biorecognition architecture based on antibody–antigen recognition. This biosensor was characterized by morphological and electrochemical techniques, achieving a linear response between 1.0 and 200 ng mL–1 and a limit of detection of 0.34 ng mL–1. Afterward, human serum samples spiked with NS1 showed recovery rates between 96.6% and 115%. All results indicate that the proposed multielectrode immunosensor is a promising, label-free, and portable diagnostic alternative for NS1 determination while maintaining a relatively low cost and simple preparation.

item.title: Machine Learning-Driven Design of Experiments for CO 2 Mineralization of Steel Slag Materials
item.description:
Abstract
The mineralization of CO2 using steel slag represents a promising pathway for simultaneous carbon sequestration and industrial-waste valorization. However, the complex and nonlinear interactions between process variables hinder the identification of the dominant mechanisms and optimal operating conditions. In this study, a hybrid modeling framework integrating artificial neural networks (ANNs) with factorial design analysis was developed to predict and interpret the performance of three key process routes: leaching, direct carbonation, and indirect carbonation. A comprehensive data set compiled from 58 published studies, comprising 171 leaching, 168 direct carbonation, and 22 indirect carbonation experiments, was used to train and validate ANN models. The trained models were subsequently employed to generate a full factorial design (3k), enabling systematic evaluation of parameter significance and interaction effects. The ANN models demonstrated strong predictive capability for leaching and acceptable performance for carbonation processes, with improved accuracy upon inclusion of reaction time, highlighting the importance of kinetic effects. The ANN–factorial analysis suggests that leaching is most strongly associated with feed composition (CaO content) and leaching agent chemistry, while direct carbonation is controlled by reaction kinetics and surface accessibility, with strong interactions between CO2 availability, pretreatment, and time. Indirect-carbonation results, which are based on the smaller data set, suggest dominant associations with solution-phase chemistry, particularly pH, Ca concentration, and precipitation kinetics, with interaction effects playing a critical role in determining carbonation efficiency. Across all processes, chemical and kinetic interactions were found to be more influential than purely physical parameters. The integration of ANN with factorial design enables the creation of a virtual experimental space, allowing comprehensive exploration of complex multivariable systems beyond experimental limitations. Steel slag mineralization exhibits a progressive shift in dominant control mechanisms, from composition-dominated behavior during leaching to coupled composition–gas-supply control during direct carbonation, and finally to solution-phase control during indirect carbonation. Comparison with our previously studied Mg-rich serpentine system further shows that the ANN–factorial framework is transferable across alkaline feedstocks, while the controlling mechanisms remain feedstock-specific: Mg-rich systems are more strongly governed by pretreatment and pH/additive chemistry, whereas steel slag systems are dominated by reactive Ca availability, CO2 supply, and Ca–carbonate precipitation chemistry. These findings provide a screening framework for process optimization and highlight the importance of material-specific modeling in CO2 mineralization technologies.

item.title: Erythrosine–Iron Oxide Nanoemulsions Combining Photodynamic Therapy with Ferroptosis-Mediated Cytotoxicity in Prostate Cancer
item.description:
Abstract
Prostate cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related death among men worldwide. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) has emerged as a promising strategy to enhance conventional treatments, yet its efficacy is often limited by poor solubility, instability, and a lack of targeting of photosensitizers. Here, we report the development of hybrid erythrosine–iron oxide nanoemulsions (MNE/Ery) produced by vacuum-assisted nanoemulsification. The optimized formulation (0.05 mg·mL–1 erythrosine; 0.5 mg·mL–1 maghemite) exhibited a hydrodynamic diameter of ∼100 nm, negative surface charge, and strong retention of the photosensitizer’s spectral profile. The iron oxide nanoparticles (20–30 nm) exhibited efficient magnetic heating potential, reaching 42 °C within 5.5 min under an alternating field (418 kHz, 12 kA·m–1), indicating suitability for future exploration in magnetic hyperthermia applications. While MNE/Ery maintained high biocompatibility toward healthy cells (HDFn and PNT2), it induced a potent light-triggered cytotoxic response in PC-3 prostate cancer cells. Upon irradiation, the platform delivered a robust, dose-dependent therapeutic effect even at conservative fluences, driven by the combination of maghemite-induced oxidative stress (ferroptosis) and erythrosine-mediated ROS generation. These findings position the MNE/Ery system as a promising nanotechnological platform for PDT with an intrinsic iron-mediated chemotherapeutic effect, with additional potential for future magnetic hyperthermia-based applications.

item.title: Natural Products against Human and Veterinary Trichomonads: From In Vitro Activity to Future Therapeutic Perspectives
item.description:
Abstract
Pathogenic trichomonads are flagellated protozoan parasites of the urogenital and digestive tracts of humans and animals. These organisms impose substantial health and economic burdens on the world. Trichomonas vaginalis causes human urogenital trichomoniasis, the most common nonviral sexually transmitted infection worldwide, and has been associated with adverse reproductive outcomes and increased risk of HIV transmission. In animals, Trichomonas gallinae causes avian trichomoniasis, a disease of the upper digestive tract that may impair feeding, compromise survival, and contribute to bird population declines, whereas Tritrichomonas foetus is responsible for bovine trichomoniasis, a major cause of cattle production losses. Despite their importance, therapeutic options remain limited. Human and avian trichomoniasis still rely on 5-nitroimidazoles, but drug resistance and regulatory restrictions have become important concerns, whereas no approved pharmacological treatment is currently available for bovine trichomoniasis, and infected animals are culled. In this context, natural products have emerged as valuable sources of new antitrichomonal agents. This Review summarizes 84 studies published between 2016 and 2026 investigating natural products against T. vaginalis, T. gallinae, and T. foetus, including plant-derived extracts and fractions, essential oils, isolated compounds, microbial metabolites, and nanotechnology-based formulations. Although several products displayed relevant antitrichomonal activity, most evidence remains restricted to in vitro studies, with comparatively few in vivo evaluations and no clinical validation of natural-product-derived candidates for trichomoniasis. Overall, natural products represent a chemically diverse and still underexplored source of antitrichomonal leads, but further validation of their selectivity, pharmacological properties, and in vivo efficacy is required before their therapeutic potential can be established.

item.title: Design and Evaluation of Fluorescent gRNAs for Visibility Improvement in dCas9-Mediated Live-Cell Imaging
item.description:
Abstract
Live-cell nuclear imaging continues to be limited by the number of fluorescent moieties that may be recruited to the DNA locus of interest. Major advances in dCas9-based live-cell imaging have been made using plasmid-based expression systems that integrate many protein fluorophores into the dCas9 fluorescent ribonucleoprotein (fRNP) complex to increase the visibility of the resulting DNA labels. The dependence on exogenous DNA plasmids, however, precludes these strategies from applications where precise control of fRNP presence is necessary or possible plasmid integration into the genome is unacceptable. In this study, we evaluated the capacity for fluorescent guide RNA (gRNA) to improve the visibility of cellular DNA labels during live-cell imaging, bypassing the need for complex fluorescent protein expression and foreign DNA plasmid delivery. Both CRISPR RNA (crRNA) and trans-activating crRNA (tracrRNA) components of the gRNA were modified with terminal cyanine 3 (Cy3) fluorophores before assembly into fRNP, and the impact on the brightness and signal-to-background (SNB) of the resulting DNA labels was evaluated at two different genomic loci: a repeat-rich Chr3 locus and chromosome telomeres. We further explored the visibility of DNA labeled with a “split” fRNP constructed from two individual tracrRNA fragments, rather than the complete 86 nt tracrRNA sequence, in order to reduce the costs and turnaround time of tracrRNA synthesis and to increase the terminal ends available for fluorophore modification. The 86 nt tracrRNA configuration bearing two terminal Cy3 modifications to both the crRNA and tracrRNA resulted in the greatest improvement to label visibility with a 190% increase in brightness and a 60% increase in SNB for both loci, on average, in comparison to the previously published fRNP containing only one Cy3 on the crRNA. The split tracrRNA fRNP was capable of labeling both genomic loci with varying success, imparting a maximum brightness improvement of 153% and an SNB improvement of 49% to Chr3 labeling, however, with no significant gains to brightness and 41% improved SNB for telomeres. For both the designs, label visibility improved consistently with additional fluorescence modification of the gRNA, indicating that the modifications were well tolerated, and further enhancement of gRNA fluorescence may continue to improve label visibility during live-cell imaging.

item.title: Dyeing and Multifunctional Finishing of Cotton Fabrics Using Ethiopian Rumex steudelii Root Extract: Response Surface Optimization, LC-MS/MS Phytochemical Profiling, and Antibacterial and UV-Protective Performance
item.description:
Abstract
Textile finishing increasingly demands sustainable, multifunctional alternatives to synthetic dyes and biocides. This study developed a single-bath, metal-free strategy to simultaneously color and biofunctionalize 100% cotton fabric using Rumex steudelii root extract. Ultrasonic-assisted extraction was optimized by response surface methodology (central composite design, CD); experimental yield ranged from 29.95% to 40.13% across the design space. The desirability-based optimum, selected to minimize temperature, time, and solvent use, was ≈55 °C, 32 min, and a 10 mL/g liquid-to-solid ratio, a predicting yield of 34.51%, which was confirmed experimentally (33.90 ± 0.18%, prediction error 1.77%). LC-MS/MS annotated 27 constituents (24 confirmed with authentic standards), dominated by flavonoids (35.38%), phenolic acids (22.25%), and anthraquinones (19.28%), providing a chemical basis for coupling coloration with bioactivity. Dyeing with the extract alone, or with citric acid or tannic acid as green cross-linkers, produced three distinct, reproducible shades (golden yellow, burnt orange, and earth brown) with color strength (K/S) of 4.42 to 10.34, and washing, rubbing, and light fastness improved to grades of 4/5–5. Cross-linked fabrics achieved excellent UV protection (UPF up to 56) and strong antibacterial activity, reducing Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli counts by up to 99.8 ± 0.23% and 97.3 ± 0.81%, respectively. By integrating RSM-optimized extraction, LC-MS/MS-resolved phytochemical mapping, and single-bath, metal-free cross-linking in one process, this work establishes Rumex steudelii as a promising platform for multifunctional natural textile finishing, with potential for scale-up pending pilot-scale validation.

item.title: Heparin-Binding Proteins in the Nanoparticle Corona: An Overlooked Player at the Bio–Nano Interface
item.description:
Abstract
When nanoparticles (NPs) enter biological environments, they rapidly acquire a layer of adsorbed proteins, known as the protein corona, which plays a central role in their interactions with cells. While extensive work has focused on how corona proteins interact with cell-surface receptors to modulate NP uptake, the role of corona–glycocalyx interactions has received comparatively little attention. In this Minireview, we highlight emerging evidence that heparin-binding proteins (HBPs) within the protein corona can engage glycosaminoglycans, such as heparan sulfate, in the cellular glycocalyx, thereby introducing an additional layer of molecular recognition at the cell surface. Drawing on recently published protein corona data sets, we further show that HBPs are frequently present and often abundant across protein coronas from diverse NP systems. These observations highlight HBPs as important, yet underappreciated, mediators of NP–cell interactions and uptake.

item.title: Novel Trilinear Flow Model for a Fractured Horizontal Well Considering Spatially Linear Decline of Fracture Conductivity
item.description:
Abstract
Pressure transient analysis (PTA) of a fractured horizontal well often relies on a trilinear flow model, but a conventional trilinear flow model assumes uniform fracture conductivity along the whole fracture length and therefore may overestimate the contribution of less-conductive fracture sections. A novel analytical trilinear flow model is proposed in this work for pressure analysis by considering a linearly declining fracture conductivity distribution from the wellbore toward the fracture tip through a new parameter (conductivity decline coefficient). The new trilinear flow problem was analytically solved in the Laplace domain, yielding a closed form solution expressed with modified Bessel functions; asymptotic limits were derived to ensure numerical stability without discretizing the fracture into multiple segments. The proposed model has been validated by comparing its results with those of the traditional trilinear flow model with uniform fracture conductivity. It is found that the conductivity decline coefficient mainly affects the middle-time transient pressure behavior by increasing the pressure and pressure derivative. Sensitivity results for CfD0 = 10 and 50 show that a decline coefficient with 1 can elevate the middle-time pressure and pressure derivative by up to 13% and 14%, respectively. The maximum fracture conductivity controls the early time pressure response, whereas well spacing and fracture spacing primarily determine the onset of late-time boundary-dominated flow. In dual-porosity SRV systems, the storativity ratio and interporosity-flow coefficient govern the timing and depth of the concave pressure derivative signature. The proposed model can provide a fast and physically interpretable PTA tool for estimating fracture/reservoir parameters, evaluating conductivity degradation, predicting production performance, and assessing spacing-controlled boundary interaction in fractured tight reservoirs.

item.title: Comparison of Alkane Distributions in Crude Oils Detected by Gas Chromatography of Whole Oils and Saturated Fractions and Gas Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry of Saturated Fractions
item.description:
Abstract
Alkane-related parameters of oils obtained by both gas chromatography (GC) and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS) were widely used in oil-source correlation. However, it is still unclear whether different detection methods will lead to significant differences in these parameters. The compositions of alkanes in Jurassic oils from the Sichuan Basin were investigated using GC analysis of whole-oil samples and saturated hydrocarbons and GC-MS analysis of saturated hydrocarbons. Comparative analyses of alkane-related parameters obtained by these detection methods were also performed in this study. n-Alkanes in the range nC3–nC35 were detected in oils using whole-oil GC analysis. By contrast, short-chain n-alkanes (nC3–nC13) were not detected by GC and GC-MS analysis of saturated hydrocarbons. The abundances of n-alkanes in the range nC14–nC16 were lower than those detected by whole-oil GC analysis. nC21–/nC22+ ratios and terrigenous/aquatic ratios (TAR = (nC27 + nC29 + nC31)/(nC15 + nC17 + nC19)) obtained by GC analysis of saturated hydrocarbons are similar to those obtained by m/z 85 mass chromatograms of GC-MS and show huge differences from those obtained by whole-oil GC analysis and total ion current of GC-MS. However, the differences between these ratios obtained by GC analysis of saturated hydrocarbons, m/z 85 mass chromatograms, and total ion current of GC-MS are systematic. Pristane/phytane (Pr/Ph) ratios obtained by GC analysis of saturated hydrocarbons exhibit little difference from those obtained by total ion current of GC-MS but show large differences from those obtained by whole-oil GC and m/z 85 mass chromatograms of GC-MS. While, the differences between Pr/Ph obtained by all these methods mentioned above are systematic and can be basically eliminated. Additionally, the different detection methods have no influence on carbon preference index, odd-to-even preference, Pr/nC17 and Ph/nC18.

item.title: Multi-Enzyme Peptide Mapping of Site-Selective Trastuzumab Modification by an Engineered Thermostable Microbial Transglutaminase
item.description:
Abstract
Peptide mapping by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) is a key analytical strategy for residue-level characterization of antibody conjugates, providing modification-site assignments and apparent relative modification estimates that complement intact-mass and chromatographic drug-to-antibody ratio (DAR) measurements. The development of homogeneous antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) relies on precise control of the conjugation site and DAR. For site-selectively modified ADCs, in which amino acid-level homogeneity is an important quality attribute, peptide mapping is therefore not only a confirmatory assay but also a central component of structural characterization. However, its reliability depends on enzymatic coverage and sample-handling conditions that affect the recovery of hydrophobic Fc-derived peptides, particularly in conjugates generated at high modification levels. In this study, we evaluated a multi-enzyme LC–MS/MS peptide-mapping workflow for antibody conjugates generated by microbial transglutaminase (MTG)-mediated Fc modification, using trastuzumab conjugated with dansylcadaverine (DNC) as a model system. An engineered thermostable MTG variant carrying five amino acid substitutions (D3C/S101P/G157S/G250R/G283C) was used to prepare a highly modified trastuzumab-DNC conjugate for evaluation of complementary protease coverage, residue-level modification-site assignment, and recovery of hydrophobic Fc-derived peptides. The engineered MTG was also compared with the commercial MTG formulation Activa using glycosylated trastuzumab under the specified nominal enzyme-loading conditions. Because this comparison was not normalized on the basis of catalytic activity under the antibody-conjugation conditions, it was treated as a formulation-based reference and was not used to establish intrinsic superiority of either enzyme preparation. Complementary digestion with trypsin, chymotrypsin, and Glu-C provided convergent evidence that DNC modification was predominantly localized to heavy-chain Q298 and enabled evaluation of other detectable glutamine-containing peptides. We further found that post-digestion addition of guanidine hydrochloride (GnHCl) during quenching increased the recovery of hydrophobic Fc-derived peptides, most notably the Q298-containing peptides. Omission of GnHCl during quenching reduced the recovery of several hydrophobic Fc-derived peptides and could bias peptide-map-based apparent modification estimates under the tested conditions. Under the optimized workflow, Q298 consistently showed the highest peptide-map-based apparent modification level, whereas apparent modification levels at other unambiguously assigned glutamine residues remained low under the tested conditions. However, these peak-area-based values do not represent absolute molar occupancy, and low-abundance off-site modifications below the analytical detection threshold cannot be excluded. These findings demonstrate that multi-enzyme peptide mapping combined with denaturant-assisted quenching provides a practical analytical workflow for residue-level characterization of highly modified, site-selective antibody conjugates. The workflow supports predominant modification at heavy-chain Q298 under the tested conditions and highlights the importance of sample-preparation optimization in peptide mapping-based characterization of ADCs and related antibody conjugates. Because DNC is a model primary amine, application of this workflow to therapeutic ADC linker-payloads will require substrate-specific optimization and analytical qualification.

item.title: One-Pot Synthesis of Pt–Fe for EOR: Effect of pH
item.description:
Abstract
The development of efficient electrocatalysts for the ethanol oxidation reaction (EOR) remains a major challenge for direct ethanol fuel cells (DEFCs) due to slow kinetics and catalyst poisoning by reaction intermediates. Herein, Pt/C and Pt–Fe/C catalysts were prepared via a one-pot polyol synthesis, and the effect of pH on Fe incorporation and catalytic performance was investigated. X-ray diffraction showed lattice contraction in Pt–Fe catalysts, confirming Fe incorporation, which was more pronounced under alkaline conditions. Electrochemical measurements demonstrated a strong dependence on both Fe addition and pH. Pt–Fe/C at pH 11.4 achieved a mass activity density of 850 A/gPt, outperforming not only Pt–Fe/C neutral and Pt/C but also the commercial Pt/C catalyst at 20 mV/s. Moreover, a lower onset potential (0.479 V) and a higher If/Ib ratio (1.9) indicate faster reaction kinetics and qualitatively suggest tolerance to adsorbed intermediates. The enhanced performance is attributed to the synergistic effect of Fe incorporation through electronic and bifunctional mechanisms.

item.title: Mechanism and Application of Imidazolium Derivatives as a Bifunctional Additive for Void-free Blind via Copper Filling
item.description:
Abstract
In conventional acidic copper electroplating, the accelerator and leveler are typically provided by different molecules, resulting in complex additive formulations and difficult-to-control intermolecular interactions. This study proposes an “intramolecular functional group division” strategy and designs a series of imidazolium salts bearing different substituents as bifunctional additives, integrating the leveling function of the imidazolium cation and the accelerating function of the pendant groups within a single molecule. Electrochemical measurements, electroplating of silicon-based micro blind vias, and multi-scale characterization demonstrate that a simplified binary system consisting solely of this additive and PEG8000 can achieve void-free superconformal filling. Systematic comparison of four imidazole derivatives containing sulfonate, cyano, and carboxyl substituents establishes a clear structure–activity relationship: the sulfonate group is the key moiety that confers the accelerating effect, Cl– bridging is a prerequisite for strong adsorption, and the structural basis for acceleration is that the sulfonate group remains exposed on the outer surface without participating in copper-surface adsorption. DFT calculations further elucidate this mechanism from the perspectives of electronic structure and adsorption configuration. This work elevates the integration of dual functions in copper electroplating additives from intermolecular synergy to the single-molecule level, providing a new paradigm for the design of multifunctional electroplating additives.

item.title: Cytoplasmic Expression of Papain Isozymes in Engineered Escherichia coli for Substrate Selectivity and Computational Insights
item.description:
Abstract
Challenges in isolating individual papain isozymes from papaya latex and in producing full-length, correctly folded, and soluble recombinant papain isozymes in Escherichia coli have limited detailed investigations into their distinct enzymatic properties and substrate specificities. In this study, we report the successful high-yield cytoplasmic expression of papain, protease omega, proteinase IV (pro-IV), and chymopapains I, II, and III in engineered E. coli SHuffle strains and a comprehensive investigation of their distinct biochemical and computational mechanistic insights. Building upon our previous work, we employed an engineered SHuffle strain using two synthetic constructs. In the first, each isozyme is translationally fused with maltose-binding protein (MBP) and expressed under engineered T7 promoters. In the second, each isozyme was co-expressed with thiol peroxidase glutathione peroxidase-7 (GPx7), and protein disulfide isomerase (PDI) pairs, yielding ∼349 mg/L soluble recombinant papain. We then hypothesized that by using this strain with the above two synthetic constructs, each isozyme would be successfully expressed as soluble proteases. Indeed, the engineered E. coli SHuffle strain produced purified papain and isozymes in yields ranging from 340 to 355 mg/L in batch fermentation. Each isozyme was kinetically characterized using two synthetic substrates, benzyloxycarbonyl-Phe-Arg-pNA and acetyl-Phe-Gly-pNA, revealing catalytic efficiencies spanning from 9.4 × 102 to 2.52 × 105 M–1 s–1 and marked differences in substrate selectivity. The optimum temperature, pH activity profiles, thermostability, and responses to metal ions were determined, revealing significant functional diversity. Structural modeling and docking studies were carried out, revealing nonconserved residues in proteinase IV that distort the active-site geometry. Site-directed mutagenesis of the conserved residues (E23G/R65G) in proteinase IV improved its catalytic function, demonstrating that active-site remodeling contributes to enhanced proteolytic activity. Together, this platform opens the door to engineering papain isozymes and variants with tailored properties for synthesizing valuable peptides, food processing, and pharmaceutical manufacturing, where enzyme purity, specificity, and optimum conditions are critical.

item.title: Biodegradable Foam Synthesized from Lignin-Rich Brewer’s Spent Grain Waste with Potential Use as a Sustainable Alternative for Packaging Applications
item.description:
Abstract
Biodegradable foams derived from agroindustrial residues provide a sustainable alternative to existing petroleum-based packaging, while supporting circular bioeconomy objectives. In this study, biofoams were synthesized using raw brewer’s spent grain (BSG1) and lignin-enriched residues (BSG2 and BSG3) obtained postfermentation for ethanol production. Chemical composition analysis of all BSG biomasses revealed that BSG1 contained 18.72% total lignin, whereas BSG2 and BSG3 exhibited substantially higher lignin contents of 78.28 and 83.69%, respectively, representing nearly a 4-fold increase. SEM (scanning electron microscopy) analysis showed an increase in biofoam porosity from BSG1 (0.4%) to BSG2 (7.8%) and BSG3 (13.4%), which correlated with enhanced compressive strength (0.49–0.50 MPa) and improved thickness recovery under uniaxial cyclic compression. It also exhibited reduced water absorption, from 20% in BSG1 to 7 and 11% in BSG2 and BSG3, respectively. The enhanced lignin content may have contributed to the strength and moisture resistance of the biofoams, whereas the relatively low water absorption of the processed BSG likely supported its degradation in the environment. The foams exhibited high solubility in river and seawater (48–70%) and near-complete soil degradation within 7–10 weeks, highlighting their rapid environmental decomposition. Thermal analysis (TG/DTG) confirmed the multistage degradation typical of lignocellulosic materials, with higher residual char in BSG2 and BSG3 reflecting their lignin-rich composition. Collectively, these results demonstrated that lignin-rich BSG residues can be transformed into mechanically robust, moderately porous, thermally stable, and rapidly biodegradable biofoams, combining enhanced strength, controlled hydrophilicity, and environmental compatibility. This work establishes a zero-waste cascade valorization strategy in which lignin-rich fermentation residues are upcycled into biodegradable biofoams, providing a sustainable pathway for replacing petroleum-based packaging materials.

item.title: RSM Optimized Feasibility Assessment of Hybrid Algae-Plastic Oil Blended Diesel Fuel with Binary Additives CuO–MgO on Performance and Emissions in CRDI Diesel Engine
item.description:
Abstract
This study was carried out to analyze the feasibility of a less-explored alternative fuel blend combination for diesel engines comprising third-generation biofuel (algae oil (AO)) and fuel derived from waste plastic. Combining these two oils in equal proportions, hybrid algae-plastic oil (HAPO) blends were formed. For this study, waste plastic oil (WPO) was produced through a lab-scale thermal pyrolysis process. The impact of different blend ratios (0–40 vol %) of HAPO-blended diesel fuel along with input engine load (20–100%) and fuel injection pressure (FIP) (300–700 bar) is experimentally tested for its performance and emission characteristics in a single-cylinder common-rail direct-injection (CRDI) diesel engine. The impact of combined total binary (CuO + MgO) metal oxide nanoadditives (0–300 ppm) in a 1:1 fixed mass ratio formulation with HAPO blends, along with engine key input variables, has also been assessed. The response surface methodology (RSM) technique was applied for optimization by developing trials using a four-factor central composite design (CCD) approach, and output responses were analyzed using surface plots. The R2 values of estimated outputs for brake thermal efficiency (BTHE), exhaust gas temperature (EGT), nitrogen oxide (NOx), smoke, and unburned hydrocarbon (HC) were determined to be nearly approaching 90–99.9%, except for the limited predictive R2 for the carbon monoxide (CO) model. The outcomes from the input parameters were optimized for maximum performance and minimum emissions. RSM-predicted optimized input value settings at 40 vol % HAPO blend, 300 ppm of total binary additive with 441.4 bar of FIP, and 52.32% engine load have given a significant RSM-predicted response of 20.27% of BTHE and 459.36 K of EGT with noticeable reduction in smoke by 11.5%, HC by 16.1 ppmv, NOx by 358.33 ppmv, and CO by 0.0927 vol % with an overall composite desirability of 81.98% within the investigated experimental domain. Final tests were conducted for experimental verification of optimized conditions by fixing the input parameters to optimized values to confirm authenticity. The percentage error between RSM-predicted values and experimental values for BTHE, EGT, smoke, and CO output responses was less than 5%, whereas for HC and NOx, the errors were 5.93 and 5.21%, respectively. The results demonstrate the short-duration laboratory-scale technical feasibility and promising performance of characterized HAPO-blended diesel as a candidate fuel for CRDI diesel engines with significant tailpipe emission reduction potential.

item.title: A Greener Acid-free Microwave-Assisted Digestion Method for Multielement Analysis of Fish Tissues by ICP–MS
item.description:
Abstract
Trace element monitoring in fish tissues requires reliable and sustainable sample preparation methods, particularly for complex biological matrices. In this study, an acid-free microwave-assisted digestion (AFMAD) method based exclusively on H2O2 was developed and optimized for multielement determination in fish tissues by ICP–MS. A central composite design coupled with response surface methodology was employed to evaluate the influence of H2O2 concentration, ramp time, and digestion temperature on matrix decomposition efficiency using 100 mg of dry fish tissue subsamples throughout the method development. The optimized conditions consisted of 30% (v/v)H2O2, 8 min ramp time, a 20 min hold time and 240 °C, resulting in residual carbon contents below 20%, which indicates efficient oxidation of the organic matrix using H2O2 in the absence of HNO3. The analytical performance of the proposed method was evaluated using cod muscle certified reference material (BCR-422), providing recoveries ranging from 76 to 101% for Fe, Cu, Zn, Mn, As, and Cd. Excellent linearity was obtained for all analytes (R2 > 0.990) within the 0–50 μg L–1 range. Limits of detection ranged from 0.0004 to 0.04 μg g–1, demonstrating suitable sensitivity for trace elemental analysis in fish matrices. The applicability of the method was demonstrated through the analysis of five commercial fish species collected in the Mariana-MG region. Concentrations of toxic elements were found in Megaleporinus conirostris (Cd, 0.003 mg kg–1) and Cichla ocellaris (As, 0.07 mg kg–1) and remained below the maximum limits established by Brazilian legislation. The proposed AFMAD method demonstrated satisfactory analytical performance for complex fish matrices while eliminating the use of concentrated mineral acids, reducing hazardous reagent consumption, and improving the sustainability characteristics of sample preparation procedures for elemental analysis.

item.title: Highly Efficient Orange-Yellow Emission in (Rb, Cs) 2 CaP 2 O 7 /Eu 2+ with Robust Thermal Stability
item.description:
Abstract
Although white light-emitting diodes (WLEDs) are the main technology in the lighting field, their advancement is limited by the need for luminescent materials with high luminous efficiency and high thermal stability, particularly in the long-wavelength region. To address this issue, in this work, a neighboring-cation substitution engineering approach is proposed and validated. Specifically, by substituting Rb+ ions with Cs+ ions, distortion of the host crystal structure is successfully induced, which further modulates the local symmetry and crystal field environment of the [CaO6] octahedron, enabling effective regulation of the Eu2+ luminescent center. Moreover, systematic investigations of the crystal structure, morphology, photoluminescence properties, and thermal quenching behavior of the as-prepared phosphors were conducted. The results indicate that both the external quantum efficiency (EQE) and thermal stability of the sample significantly improved after Cs+ substitution. Furthermore, by combining the as-synthesized orange-yellow phosphor with commercial blue-emitting BaMgAl10O17/Eu2+ (BAM: Eu2+) and green-emitting (Ba,Sr)2SiO4/Eu2+ phosphors, a high-performance WLED device was fabricated. The performance of this device was evaluated to validate its applicability in practical lighting, and the potential of this material for field emission displays (FEDs) was also explored. This work provides a new material system and structural design approach for developing Eu2+-activated phosphate-based orange-yellow phosphors with high efficiency and thermal stability.

item.title: Selective Functionalization of Graphene Oxide Unlocks Synergistic Catalysis for Organophosphate Degradation
item.description:
Abstract
Site-selective functionalization of nanomaterials such as graphene oxide (GO) is a powerful strategy to tailor catalytic performance, with the degree and positioning of functional groups being critical for targeted applications. Herein, we present a systematic study on the functionalization of GO with ethylenediamine through two distinct pathways: (i) attachment at carboxylic acid groups located at the sheet edges and (ii) attachment at epoxide groups distributed across the basal plane. Comprehensive characterization, including XPS, AFM-IR, among others, was consistent with the site-specific functionalization. Importantly, the positioning effect was directly correlated with catalytic activity in the heterogeneous degradation of hazardous organophosphates─compounds widely used in agrochemicals and notorious for their extreme toxicity and persistence in the environment. Our results reveal that functionalization at the epoxide sites, despite yielding a lower degree of modification, produced superior catalytic efficiency, achieving a rate constant of 4.86 min–1 g–1, in contrast to 0.721 min–1 g–1 for the nanocatalyst functionalized via the carboxylic acid. The higher catalytic rate constant was obtained due to synergistic interactions with freely available carboxylic acids acting as intramolecular catalysts. Blocking these carboxylic acids with inert groups led to a marked decrease in activity, emphasizing their mechanistic role. Beyond advancing toward functionalization strategies, this study demonstrates how nanodesign can be leveraged to probe catalytic mechanisms and enhance detoxification of organophosphates. Understanding these synergistic effects in GO-based materials opens new avenues for designing nanocatalysts aimed at mitigating the dual-use hazards of organophosphates, with broad implications for environmental remediation and public health protection.

item.title: Vacuum Drying Maintains the Integrity of DNA and Protects the Stability of PCR Amplification under Accelerated Aging
item.description:
Abstract
DNA, with its advantages such as ultrahigh storage density, low energy consumption, and ultralong potential lifespan, has become a new generation of storage medium with great development potential. The stability of DNA storage directly determines the reliability of information retrieval. Conventional cryopreservation not only incurs high costs but also leads to DNA degradation over long-term storage. Although current DNA protection methods can delay degradation to some extent, they can hinder DNA release and interfere with downstream PCR amplification and sequencing processes. In this study, solid DNA samples were prepared using vacuum drying without exogenous additives, and accelerated aging experiments were conducted at 70 °C to investigate the integrity of DNA and the stability of PCR amplification. We found that vacuum-dried DNA maintained excellent integrity after being heated for 40 h. DNA heated for 0–30 h showed no significant difference in cycle threshold (Ct) values compared with the unheated control, even after 1000-fold dilution. A significant increase in the Ct value was observed only under critical conditions, in which the DNA sample was heated for 40 h and diluted 1000 times. Under different drying temperatures, the effects of 50 °C vacuum drying and lyophilization on protecting DNA stability are comparable. Our research provides important insights into the storage of long templates and the preservation of nucleic acid samples in fields such as medicine and forensic science.

item.title: Mineral-Enriched Biochars from Co-Pyrolysis of Sewage Sludge, Sawdust, and Basaltic Rocks: Soil Amendment Potential and Carbon Stability
item.description:
Abstract
Co-pyrolysis of sewage sludge (SS) and sawdust (SD) with basaltic minerals may produce nutrient-enriched biochars for soil amendment and long-term carbon (C) persistence. However, the effects of mineral incorporation on C transformations and the interpretation of conventional stability indices remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we compared SS and SD copyrolyzed with zeolitic basalt (ZB) and metabasalt (MB). The resulting materials, produced at 500 °C, were characterized by proximate and elemental analyses, X-ray diffraction, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and nutrient and carbon-stability assessments. Mineral addition increased biochar yields to 70–73%, whereas SD-derived biochar exhibited the highest fixed C and thermostable fractions. Materials obtained by co-pyrolyzing SD with ZB or MB, and SS with ZB, showed high thermal resistance. Mineral-enriched biochars had higher ash contents and contained silicate-rich phases, modifying their mineralogical composition and nutrient profiles. Co-pyrolysis of SS with basaltic materials increased Ca, Mg, P, and micronutrient contents. Contrasting responses among elemental, thermochemical, and persistence-based indices showed that no single approach adequately evaluates C stability in mineral-enriched biochars. These findings support the potential use of mineral-enriched biochars as soil amendments and show that C stability requires integrated evaluation.

item.title: A Validated SEM-EDS Workflow for Screening Rare High-Mg Minerals in Fine-Grained Chang’e-6 Lunar Soil
item.description:
Abstract
Accurate localization of rare high-Mg minerals in lunar soil is hindered by their small grain size and occurrence in compositionally heterogeneous matrices. High-Mg minerals are operationally defined as olivine with Fo > 80 (Fo = 100 × Mg/(Mg + FeT) molar basis), orthopyroxene with Mg# > 80 (Mg# = 100 × Mg/(Mg + FeT) molar basis), and clinopyroxene with Mg# > 70. A particle-resolved scanning electron microscopy-energy dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) screening method was developed for Chang’e-6 lunar soil. The key advance is that Mg-bearing particles are not only identified by phase mapping but are further classified according to Mg# for pyroxene and Fo for olivine, enabling high-Mg candidates to be directly ranked and spatially located across large mapped areas. Analytical conditions were optimized using Monte Carlo simulations, counting-statistics requirements, particle-size constraints, and phase-segmentation performance. The final conditions were 15 kV, 10 nA, a dwell time of 2000 μs, a resolution of 1024 pixels, frame processing of 4, a boundary tolerance of 10, and a grouping level of 0. Quantitative SEM-EDS results agreed well with electron-probe microanalysis (EPMA) analyses of the same grains. Application of the method showed that Mg-bearing phases accounted for approximately 1.8% of the mapped compositional area and enabled rapid localization of high-Mg olivine and pyroxene grains for subsequent high-precision analyses. The workflow provides a practical basis for selecting high-Mg candidates for subsequent studies of lunar mantle provenance and Lunar Magma Ocean differentiation.

item.title: Fungal-Derived Biobased Filaments for Textile Applications: Effect of Plasticizer and Cross-Linking Agent
item.description:
Abstract
Fungal cell wall polymers derived from food waste have recently emerged as a renewable platform for novel biobased fibers. In this study, fungal biomass of Rhizopus delemar cultivated on bread waste was processed to isolate the alkali-insoluble cell wall material rich in chitin and chitosan, which was converted into a hydrogel spinning dope for dry gel spinning of continuous filaments. A molecular design strategy was employed to tailor filament performance using vanillin as a biobased cross-linker and glycerol as a plasticizer. The impact of these modifications on the properties of the filaments was systematically evaluated. Vanillin provided only marginal improvement in tenacity, suggesting that its incorporation did not substantially reinforce the chitosan-rich network. In contrast, glycerol incorporation significantly enhanced filament ductility and reduced brittleness during postspinning deformation processes such as twisting, thereby enabling stable yarn formation, although with a reduction in tensile strength. Multifilament yarns were successfully fabricated, and knitted textile specimens were produced for the first time from fungal-derived yarns, demonstrating structural integrity under textile processing conditions. This study establishes a structure–property framework for balancing stiffness and flexibility in fungal-based filaments and advances their development toward engineered, renewable textile materials.

item.title: Cross-Linking Simulation at Metal Oxide-Thermoset Interfaces Using Quantum Chemical and Molecular Dynamics Methods
item.description:
Abstract
Understanding how oxidized metal surfaces catalyze the curing of epoxy resins is essential in improving the reliabilities of epoxy-metal oxide interfaces in multimaterial systems. The catalytic effects of hydroxylated oxidized tin metal (SnO2) surfaces on the cross-linking of epoxy resins were investigated using a hybrid approach that combined quantum chemical calculations with molecular dynamics simulations, wherein the reaction kinetics were modeled using Monte Carlo techniques. Analyzing the reaction pathways and spatial distributions at different hydroxylation levels revealed that fully hydroxylated SnO2 surfaces promoted surface-initiated curing, whereas partially hydroxylated surfaces led to more dispersed reaction propagation. These results highlight the critical roles of the interfacial OH groups in regulating the reaction kinetics, cross-linking density, and polymer network structure. In addition to these mechanistic insights, this study establishes a generalizable methodology for use in probing curing reactions at epoxy-metal oxide interfaces, and it clarifies how metal oxidation states govern interfacial catalysis. Critically, it bridges atomic-scale mechanisms with macroscopic interfacial reliability, addressing the broader question of how the interfacial chemistry dictates the formation and performance of a thermoset network. The conclusions further indicate that surface hydroxylation can be used to regulate the curing efficiency and cross-link distribution, which is critical in rationally designing epoxy formulations and surface treatments.

item.title: The Impact of Semimetallic Bismuth Electrical Contacts on Optical Properties of a MoS 2 Monolayer
item.description:
Abstract
Achieving high performance in transition-metal dichalcogenide-based optoelectronic devices is challenging because the realization of an efficient electrical contacting scheme should not be obtained at the expense of their optical quality. Here, we present the results of optical studies of MoS2 monolayers that have been electrically contacted with bismuth and gold. The photoluminescence (PL) spectra of the samples contacted with both materials are significantly broadened. In the case of the bismuth-contacted sample, we observe an additional low-energy band in the PL spectrum, which we attribute to a defect state formed during the evaporation of Bi. Comparison of the intensities of the excitonic peak and the defect-related peak reveals that there is a correlation between the type of contacts and the optical properties of the contacted material.

item.title: Chemically Powered High-Aspect-Ratio Cilia with Tunable Biomimetic Motion
item.description:
Abstract
Cilia are ubiquitous biological actuators that drive essential functions ranging from clearing contaminants from mammalian lungs to enabling locomotion and feeding in microorganisms. Their utility has inspired the development of artificial cilia. Yet while natural cilia operate through the conversion of chemical energy to mechanical motion, most artificial cilia made to date are externally powered using various fields. Most of these systems have also been of relatively low aspect ratios in comparison to their biological counterparts. In this work we report the synthesis and characterization of chemically powered, high-aspect-ratio artificial cilia with microscale diameters that exhibit individually autonomous, biomimetic oscillatory motion. Actuated using an oscillatory chemical reaction, the reaction catalyst is incorporated into the soft cilia hydrogel material where periodic oxidation and reduction of the catalyst induced periodic swelling and deswelling to generate motion. A customizable, 3D printed mold-based fabrication strategy is developed. The catalyst distribution, concentration, and cilium cross-sectional geometry are systematically varied across representative discrete levels to assess their influence on motion. The results show that motion is strongly governed by the interplay between catalyst loading and geometric asymmetry. Increasing the catalyst-containing stalk fraction and catalyst concentration enhances oscillation amplitude and motion regularity, whereas lower catalyst concentrations favor faster oscillatory dynamics. Geometric asymmetry enhances the speed, amplitude and periodic regularity of motion of these low Reynolds number structures. These findings demonstrate tunable motion in chemically driven artificial cilia and establish a framework for the design of biomimetic, chemically powered microscale actuators with potential applications in soft robotics.

item.title: Abundant Reaction Mechanisms for the α-Nucleophile-Involved Reaction of HOO – + CH 3 Br
item.description:
Abstract
The reaction of the peroxide ion with CH3Br was investigated by direct dynamics simulation. A variety of reaction mechanisms, i.e., front-side complex, proton exchange, and H-migration mechanisms, were found, and the nature of these mechanisms was discussed in detail, which is essential for the dynamical behavior of diatomic or triatomic nucleophilic substitution reactions involving an α-nucleophile. Furthermore, the dynamic characteristics of X– + CH3Y reactions (X= HOO and OH; Y = Cl, Br, and I) were compared to reveal the influences of the nucleophile and leaving group on the α-nucleophile reactions. Atomistic reaction mechanism analyses find that HOO– + CH3Br collisions show similar reaction probabilities to the HO– + CH3Br reaction, although the proton affinity of HO– is larger than that of HOO–, which reveals the enhanced reactivity of HOO– and the presence of an α-effect relative to the normal nucleophiles. For the HOO– + CH3Br reaction, the indirect mechanisms are dominant at low collision energy, and a dramatic transition from complex-mediated indirect to direct occurs when changing HOO– to the normal nucleophile HO–. Besides, with the leaving group ability trend of Cl < Br, the branching ratio of the direct mechanism increases from 7 to 17%, and simultaneously, the ratio of the indirect mechanism decreases, which is attributed to the lower central barrier and an “earlier” transition state for the HOO– + CH3Br reaction.

item.title: Vegetation-Associated Mercury Patterns and Biogeochemical Signals in a Tropical Urban Mining Region
item.description:
Abstract
To evaluate vegetation-associated mercury (Hg) loading in tropical regions affected by artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM), we quantified total mercury (HgT) in canopy leaves and leaf litter of Licania tomentosa across an ASGM-impacted urban center, Peixoto de Azevedo (PEI), and two lower-exposure reference sites: Nova Santa Helena (ASH) and a native forest fragment (ANM). Canopy leaves reached up to 543 μg kg–1 near gold-buying shops, with probabilistic modeling identifying a high-concentration subpopulation extending to 607 μg kg–1. Leaf litter consistently exhibited higher HgT than paired canopy leaves (RatioC = 1.39–4.70; mean = 3.15), indicating relative enrichment during senescence. Spatial interpolation suggested sharply localized vegetation-associated Hg hotspots within ∼300 m of gold-trading units, superimposed on a heterogeneous urban baseline. The regional baseline was defined using ASH, where HgT concentrations ranged from 6.82 to 35.31 μg kg–1 after excluding a single transport-related outlier. These results demonstrate that gold-trading corridors are plausible localized contributors to elevated HgT in urban vegetation and may produce Hg-enriched biomass that can enter municipal waste streams. This framework provides a high-resolution, low-cost approach for Hg surveillance in tropical ASGM regions and offers chemically grounded insight into vegetation-associated Hg patterns and biogeochemical partitioning in urban environments.

item.title: Membrane Charge and Packing Govern the Interfacial Insertion, Structure, and Dynamics of Ctx(Ile 21 )-Ha and Its TOAC-Labeled Analogues in Biomimetic Liposomes
item.description:
Abstract
Cationic antimicrobial peptides are promising candidates to combat antifungal resistance. However, a detailed understanding of their membranotropic activity is required for targeted applications and sequence engineering. Here, we investigated the native peptide Ctx(Ile21)-Ha, derived from the Brazilian Cerrado tree frog Boana albopunctata, and its analogues site-specifically labeled with the paramagnetic amino acid TOAC (2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine-N-oxyl-4-amino-4-carboxylic acid). Peptide interactions with biomimetic monolayers and liposomes mimicking human, fungal, and bacterial membranes were investigated using Langmuir monolayers, circular dichroism, and electron spin resonance (ESR). Anionic lipids, particularly palmitoyl-oleoyl-phosphatidylglycerol (POPG) and palmitoyl-oleoyl-phosphatidylserine (POPS), strongly enhanced peptide penetration into lipid monolayers and promoted substantial α-helical folding in large unilamellar vesicles (LUVs). The distinct monolayer responses of POPG- and POPS-containing membranes, despite their comparable α-helical contents, indicate that anionic headgroup chemistry modulates peptide–membrane interactions beyond electrostatic attraction. Conversely, cholesterol and ergosterol reduced peptide penetration and attenuated membrane-induced helix formation due to sterol-induced membrane packing. Site-directed ESR revealed lipid-dependent motional regimes for [TOAC2]Ctx(Ile21)-Ha and [TOAC13]Ctx(Ile21)-Ha, with the central region of the peptide becoming substantially more immobilized than the N-terminus upon membrane interaction. CD-derived membrane-association isotherms further showed that anionic membranes favor the coupled association/folding response, whereas comparison across the complementary techniques indicates that membrane association, peptide folding, and membrane penetration are mechanistically related but distinct steps in peptide–membrane interactions. Overall, the membrane activity of Ctx(Ile21)-Ha is best described as a charge- and packing-modulated process, in which electrostatic interactions favor peptide binding and folding, whereas membrane order modulates membrane penetration and local peptide dynamics.

item.title: Effect of Passive Prechamber and Direct Water Injection on Performance and Efficiency Improvement within a Gasoline Engine
item.description:
Abstract
With the increasingly stringent global energy-saving policies, gasoline engines are facing great challenges, and how to achieve high efficiency in gasoline engines has become an urgent technical challenge. Passive prechamber technology can partially enhance the thermal efficiency of high-load, high-compression-ratio engines under lean-burn conditions, but its effectiveness in reducing NOx emissions is limited. In contrast, the introduction of direct water injection (DWI) technology can further optimize thermal efficiency under lean-burn conditions while significantly lowering NOx emissions. Through three-dimensional flow simulation analysis coupled with detailed chemical reaction mechanism, the engine combustion characteristics under stoichiometric conditions and lean-burn conditions are systematically investigated in this paper by the effect of passive prechamber jet ignition combined with direct water injection. It is shown by the results that CA50 can be effectively advanced, degree of constant-volume combustion can be improved, and efficiency improvement can be realized by this technical solution. Under stoichiometric conditions, optimization of the spark timing increased the indicated thermal efficiency from the baseline value of 34.69% to 39.75%; however, the NOx emissions under this condition increased by 26.01% compared with the baseline. At λ = 1.4, optimization of the spark timing increased the indicated thermal efficiency from the baseline value of 34.69% to 44.82%, while the NOx emissions were reduced by 67.28% relative to the baseline. Compared with stoichiometric operation, the combination of a passive PC and DWI under lean-burn conditions substantially reduces the knock tendency, enabling higher thermal efficiency together with lower emissions.

item.title: Effects of Drying on the Properties and Applications of Alkaline Corn Cob Lignin
item.description:
Abstract
Lignins are macromolecules obtained from plant biomass with great potential for high-value industrial applications. However, gaps remain regarding how lignin processing, particularly drying, affects its valorization. This study investigated how different drying techniques affect the physicochemical and biological properties of corn cob lignin, including color, UV-blocking ability, antioxidant activity, antimicrobial potential, and toxicity. Lignin was extracted via alkaline pretreatment, and the suspension was dried using four methods: freeze-drying (L), spouted bed at 60 °C (SB), oven at 60 °C (O60), and oven at 105 °C (O105). UV analysis confirmed that air exposure and temperature increases led to condensation reactions due to the loss of phenolic hydroxyl groups. Interestingly, spouted bed drying preserved the original color and maintained a phenolic hydroxyl content similar to freeze-drying, while exhibiting the highest antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive bacteria. Oven-dried lignins (O60 and O105) showed enhanced UV-blocking capabilities and superior in vitro DPPH radical scavenging but displayed lower ABTS inhibition efficiency (∼0.02 mg/mL vs 0.012 mg/mL for L). No correlation was observed between the lignin drying method and the zebrafish survival rate within the studied range (up to 100 mg/L). These findings demonstrate that drying techniques can strategically modulate lignin functional properties, serving as a crucial processing step for developing macromolecular functional products.

item.title: Recyclability of Oxime Resin in Solid-Phase Peptide Synthesis
item.description:
Abstract
Greener approaches are essential to significantly reduce the environmental impact of solid phase peptide synthesis (SPPS). In this regard, we report a systematic study on the sustainable use of the Kaiser-DeGrado oxime resin. The reusability efficiency of this polystyrene-based resin was investigated through the synthesis of linear and cyclic model peptides with different structural features. We demonstrated that the oxime resin can be reused over multiple SPPS cycles without any special treatment, while still affording crude peptides in good purity and yield even after eight cycles. Furthermore, regeneration of the resin improved its efficiency approaching performances comparable to those of the freshly prepared resin. In addition, the same resin can be reused multiple times within a single reaction vessel using significantly fewer reagents and solvents, reducing material expenditures and waste while simplifying workflow.

item.title: Evaluating the Slow-Release Fertilizer Effects of Calcium Potassium Phosphates from Mechanochemically Treated Calcium Carbonate Materials with KH 2 PO 4
item.description:
Abstract
Developing slow-release fertilizers, carefully adjusting their solubility profiles, is an important way to improve nutrient use efficiency and potentially reduce environmental impacts associated with nutrient losses and accumulation in water bodies, such as potential eutrophication. In this work, CaCO3 from industrial byproducts (spent lime, i.e., carbokalk, and eggshells) was mechanochemically activated with KH2PO4 and citric acid as an additive. X-ray diffraction indicated the formation of calcium potassium phosphate phases, along with residual CaCO3, depending on milling conditions. However, citric acid addition suppressed crystalline phosphate formation, likely influencing species organization and favoring poorly crystalline or amorphous phosphate phases, possibly through Ca complexation. Phosphorus percolation from milled samples remained low at early stages (0.2–4% after 2 days) and reached only 21–35% after 7 days, whereas potassium showed faster release, with 0.2–10% at 2 days and up to ∼100% percolation after 7 days. Greenhouse trials with Brachiaria brizantha over three harvest cycles suggested improved nutrient management, evidenced by a more gradual biomass increase and nutrient uptake, in contrast to the early peak and subsequent decline observed in positive controls using KH2PO4 and triple superphosphate (TSP). Thus, mechanochemical processing offers a smarter product capable of gradually releasing its fertilizer content, offering a promising route toward efficient and sustainable fertilization strategies.

item.title: Weighted Views Representation with Multi-Head Coulomb Attention for Molecular Property Prediction
item.description:
Abstract
We extend the weighted-views molecular featurization framework (d’Avezac, Botts, Mohlenkamp, and Zunger, 2011) by enriching it with single-atom properties and Coulomb pair information. We use these enriched views within a machine-learning architecture incorporating shared Transformers whose attention scores directly incorporate Coulomb interactions, weighted aggregation of view outputs, and a final prediction neural network. We demonstrate performance competitive with the state-of-the-art on the QM7 atomization energy benchmark (regression), ranking enantiomers by their docking scores (trained as regression, tested by ranking), lipophilicity (regression), and blood–brain barrier penetration (classification).

item.title: Retraction of “ Toxicity of Nanoscaled Zero-Valent Iron Particles on Tilapia, Oreochromis mossambicus ”
item.description: The authors retract “Toxicity of Nanoscaled Zero-Valent Iron Particles on Tilapia, Oreochromis mossambicus” (DOI: 10.1021/acsomega.2c05696) because there is overlap between panels A, B and C in Figure 4, indicating that the images were taken from the same sample. The authors provided image files during the post-publication review process; however, sufficient confidence in the relationship of the data to the results reported in the article was not assured. This undermines the reliability of the results presented. As such, the article is being retracted.

Abstract
We present a differential-geometric formulation of chemical reaction dynamics in which the nuclear configuration space is treated as a curved manifold whose metric is induced by the covariant Hessian of the potential energy surface (PES). In this Riemannian setting, reaction pathways emerge as geodesics of a curvature-weighted action, providing an intrinsic, coordinate-independent alternative to steepest-descent and chain-of-states methods. The second variation of the action δ2S furnishes a rigorous stability index that identifies transition states as regions of negative sectional curvature and links vibrational structure directly to curvature eigenvalues through the Jacobi operator. The transition state (TS) corresponds intrinsically to a region where the manifold’s signature becomes pseudo-Riemannian, characterized by local instability where δ2S < 0. Furthermore, the linearization of the geodesic equation yields a Jacobi operator, whose eigenvalues reproduce harmonic and anharmonic vibrational frequencies, directly connecting spectroscopic data to curvature invariants. Applied to the dissociation channels of water (H2O → H + OH) and (H2O → H2 + O), this framework reproduces fundamental vibrational frequencies, rotational constants, and anharmonicities with 1–5% accuracy and generates detailed stability maps that resolve hyperbolic, parabolic, and elliptic regions along the minimal path. Beyond reproducing known mechanistic information, the formalism reveals geometric features─channel anisotropy, curvature-driven bifurcations, and instability corridors─that remain hidden in traditional approaches. By reframing reaction dynamics through intrinsic geometry rather than extrinsic coordinates, this work lays the foundation for a unified geometric description of reaction pathways, stability, and spectroscopy.

item.title: Melt-Processed AgNP-LDPE Nanocomposites with Balanced Antimicrobial and Mechanical Performance for Livestock-Farming Applications
item.description:
Abstract
Bacterial contamination in livestock-farming and reproductive-management environments creates a need for antimicrobial polymer materials with reliable processability, mechanical performance, and application-related compatibility. In this study, poly(vinylpyrrolidone) (PVP)-stabilized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) were synthesized and incorporated into low-density polyethylene (LDPE) using a masterbatch-based melt-processing approach. AgNP formation was confirmed by UV–vis spectroscopy, TEM, and FTIR. The synthesized AgNPs showed antimicrobial activity against bacterial isolates from boar semen and sow vaginal discharge, and time-kill analysis demonstrated time- and dose-dependent bacterial inhibition. A 25 kg AgNP-rich LDPE masterbatch was prepared by industrial-scale extrusion, and diluted to produce the AgNP-LDPE nanocomposites containing 50, 100, and 500 ppm AgNPs. The nanocomposites were evaluated in terms of Ag distribution, mechanical properties, thermal behavior, Ag+ release, antibacterial activity, boar semen quality, and fertility performance in sows. Loadings of 50 and 100 ppm maintained or improved tensile performance, whereas 500 ppm reduced tensile strength and ductility. The 50 and 100 ppm nanocomposites exhibited progressive Ag+ release and strong antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The semen tubes containing 50 and 100 ppm AgNPs showed no significant adverse effects on sperm motility, progressive motility, pregnancy rate, or farrowing rate. These results identify 50–100 ppm as an effective loading range for melt-processed AgNP-LDPE nanocomposites with balanced antimicrobial performance, mechanical properties, and application-related compatibility for livestock-farming applications.

item.title: Polyacetylenes from Lobelia chinensis with Dermal Papilla Cell Proliferative Activity and Their Enhanced Production through Elicitation
item.description:
Abstract
Lobelia chinensis is a medicinal plant containing a wide variety of bioactive constituents. In the present study, a 50% methanol extract of L. chinensis significantly promoted the proliferation of human dermal papilla (DP) cells. The n-BuOH fraction was identified as the most active fraction, from which eight compounds were isolated and identified as four polyacetylenes, lobetyolinin (1), lobetyolin (2), pratiallin B (3), and tangshenyne B (4), two lignans, dehydrodiconiferyl alcohol 4-O-β-D-glucopyranoside (5) and urolignoside (6), and two nitrogen-containing compounds, tryptophan (7) and adenosine (8). Six compounds (1–4, 6, and 7) significantly stimulated DP cell proliferation, indicating that polyacetylenes are major contributors to the biological activity of L. chinensis. To enhance the production of the major active polyacetylenes, in vitro shoot cultures were treated with various elicitors. Quantitative HPLC analysis demonstrated elicitor-dependent changes in the accumulation of lobetyolinin (1) and lobetyolin (2), with 100 mg L–1 yeast extract producing the highest levels of both compounds. Extracts from elicitor-treated cultures also exhibited enhanced DP cell proliferative activity compared with untreated cultures, suggesting that the enhanced biological activity is associated with coordinated changes in multiple bioactive constituents rather than with the increased accumulation of a single compound. These findings identify major polyacetylenes contributing to the DP cell proliferative activity of L. chinensis and link their biological activity with elicitor-assisted metabolite production, providing a practical strategy for the sustainable production of standardized L. chinensis materials with potential hair-growth-promoting applications.

item.title: Development of Supramolecular Calix[4]arene-MCM-Based Nanomaterials Doped with CuNPs: An Inorganic–Organic Hybrid Recyclable Nanoenzyme as a Potent Peroxidase and Oxidase Mimic
item.description:
Abstract
An inorganic–organic hybrid nanomaterial, Cu@MCMCal, was synthesized by immobilizing p-tert-butyl calix[4]arene on to mesoporous silica followed by incorporation of CuNPs. The synthesized nanomaterial was characterized extensively using various analytical techniques such as FT-IR, UV–Vis spectroscopy, TEM, PXRD, XPS, Cu LMM Auger, BET, and TGA analyses. The hybrid nanomaterial was evaluated for its catalytic performance toward peroxidase-like activity using 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) and o-phenylenediamine (OPD) as a substrate at room temperature at pH 4.5 in acetate buffer and pH 7.4 in PBS buffer, respectively. Enzyme kinetics was performed for both the substrates using the Michaelis–Menten steady-state kinetics and the Lineweaver–Burk plot to determine the catalytic affinity. Based on the kinetic measurements, the values of the Km for TMB and OPD were found to be 0.661 ± 0.143 and 0.606 ± 0.061 mM, respectively. The hybrid nanoenzyme also exhibits the oxidase-like activity using dopamine as a substrate at pH 7.4 in PBS buffer. The Cu@MCMCal nanomaterial acted as a nanoenzyme, efficient for catalysis toward oxidation reactions with better cost effectiveness and improved stability and recyclability as compared to biological enzymes. Therefore, a promising, stable, efficient, and robust nanoenzyme has been development for oxidation reactions.

item.title: Resource Analysis and Screening for Potential CO 2 Storage Targets in Low-Porosity Saline Aquifers, Yulin, China
item.description:
Abstract
The Ordos Basin, a crucial energy base in China, leads the nation in oil, gas, and coal production, consequently leading to high carbon emissions. This establishes it as a key prospective region for implementing CO2 geological storage (CCS) to facilitate regional emissions reductions. However, the basin is predominantly characterized by low-porosity and ultralow-permeability reservoirs, which limit the applicability of current site selection criteria, largely derived from successful international projects involving high-porosity and high-permeability reservoirs. There is a lack of systematic site selection research tailored to such low-quality reservoirs. Therefore, this study focuses on screening target areas for the CO2 storage. On the basis of well-logging and geological data from 192 wells in the Yulin area of the Ordos Basin, we systematically conducted lithostratigraphic correlation, reservoir property interpretation, and deep saline aquifer identification. This resulted in the identification of two saline aquifers: the Chang 10-3 Submember of the Yanchang Formation (with an average porosity of 8.3% and a maximum permeability of 12.3 mD) and the Qian 5 Member of the Shiqianfeng Formation (with an average porosity of 8.5% and a maximum permeability of 8.3 mD). We then developed the low-porosity and low-permeability evaluation index system (LOWEIS), a dedicated framework integrating and quantifying more than ten key indicators, including the sand-to-formation ratio, single-layer thickness, porosity, permeability, shale-to-formation ratio, and social environmental constraints. Applying the LOWEIS for hierarchical evaluation and spatial overlay analysis across the 14,000 km2 area of Yulin, China, we preliminarily identified 8 favorable storage targets with the highest implementation potential. This work complements existing site selection techniques for CO2 geological storage and provides a targeted evaluation framework for low-porosity and low-permeability saline aquifers.

item.title: Migration Mechanisms and Spatial Differentiation of Elements in Coal under Stress Action
item.description:
Abstract
Tectonic stress is an important factor that controls elemental migration in coal. However, the mechanisms underlying stress-induced elemental migration and the factors controlling the resulting spatial differentiation remain poorly understood. In this study, high-temperature and high-pressure simulation experiments were employed as the primary approach. By integrating the macroscopic deformation characteristics of coal with the evolution of its molecular structure at the microscopic scale, we investigated the stress-induced migration mechanisms and spatial differentiation characteristics of the elements in coal.
